summary.headline: Welspun Corp Q2 FY27 EBITDA hit a record INR782 crore (+25% YoY) with order book near INR50,000 crore and net cash of INR3,887 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 EBITDA of INR782 crore (+25% YoY) and H1 EBITDA of INR1,538 crore (+30% YoY), both all-time highs, against FY27 guidance of INR2,850 crore. Order book stands at a record ~INR50,000 crore (~USD 5.2 billion), with the US booked through FY29. The Board approved three investments: a US spiral pipe debottlenecking (225,000 MTPA, up to USD 115 million, ready by March 2028), a 50-50 Jordan spiral pipe and coating plant with Perma-Pipe (up to USD 125 million), and an India FBE coating JV with Perma-Pipe (about INR110 crore). Domestic India demand, especially water, remains weak, while exports and the US remain the growth drivers.

segments.name: US (Little Rock spiral pipe)
segments.commentary: Booked through FY29 with a INR5,500 crore data-centre pipeline order recently won; 800-acre site with port and rail access cited as a cost and speed advantage. US EBITDA per tonne called exceptional versus a sustainable ~$300/tonne, and current US order margins are locked in through FY29 per management.

segments.name: Saudi Arabia (LSAW and DI pipe)
segments.commentary: Commissioning on track, with LSAW and DIP plants to be completed in Q3 and up and running by year-end; order materialisation delayed by Middle East supply chain disruption. Management targets at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year, and noted anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: India domestic DI and line pipe
segments.commentary: Domestic water demand under stress and Jal Jeevan Mission budget slowdown; domestic DI volumes to be substantially lower. Management is shifting DI production toward exports (Europe, Middle East) and reported that pig iron performed well.

segments.name: India exports
segments.commentary: Management called exports the bright spot, with bid pipeline robust for Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia and LatAm, all serviced from India.

segments.name: Welspun Specialty Solutions (WSSL)
segments.commentary: Stainless steel bars and seamless pipes; Q2 exports to Europe hit by freight costs and tariffs, and domestic demand expected to improve over the next two quarters. Power gen, nuclear, defence, aerospace, oil and gas and petrochemicals are the focus sectors.

segments.name: Sintex
segments.commentary: Focused on premiumisation in water tanks and on plastic pipes, now in 15 states. Management said the fintech/Sintex loss was driven by marketing, R&D and digital investment, and that it is close to breakeven before those costs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR2,850 crore retained; management said H2 is tracking well and it would be pleasantly surprised to exceed guidance, but stayed cautious.
ROCE guidance is more than 20% for FY27; H1 annualised ROCE is 22.7%.
Saudi plant readiness expected in Q3 FY27; incremental earnings from new US and Saudi capacity expected from FY28, with a possible lag if the Middle East supply chain does not normalise.
Jordan capacity is being finalised at about 350,000 to 500,000 tonnes, against a firm MoU and an existing order backlog.
Company expects to remain in net cash after all announced capex (Saudi, US, Jordan, India JV).
capex_capacity: US spiral pipe debottlenecking and capacity augmentation: 225,000 MTPA at up to USD 115 million, ready by March 2028.

Jordan greenfield spiral pipe and coating plant, 50-50 JV with Perma-Pipe, total capex up to USD 125 million, backed by a firm MoU with the Jordan National Water Carrier developers and the government.
India FBE coating JV with Perma-Pipe at Anjar, about INR110 crore total project cost, expected to be operational in the next financial year.
Saudi LSAW and DIP plants in final commissioning, targeted for Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: US demand is robust with a strong bid pipeline (data centres, LNG exports, gas-fired captive power). Management said ordering is being calibrated, with some projects still to be finalised over the next couple of quarters, and expects demand to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29.

Total contested bid pipeline is about 2 to 3 million tonnes at any time, against a typical 3 to 4 million tonnes; India domestic bid pipeline described as weak, while India export and Saudi pipelines are robust.
Saudi DIP demand is seen as import substitution, with only about two-thirds of captive DI requirement currently served by imports; Welspun expects first right of refusal on local demand.
Management described US and Middle East demand as structural rather than cyclical, with 5 to 7 years of visibility.
Competition in the US from 2 to 3 players, who are mainly doing debottlenecking; Saudi line pipe competition is pre-existing and rising, and Welspun is targeting niche segments there.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers ordering beyond FY29 in the US, and how should order build-up be viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline remains robust but ordering is being calibrated in timing; intensity will slow, but demand is expected to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new Saudi and Jordan capacity fungible to the US if US demand stays high?
qa_highlights.answer: Fungibility exists technically, but Saudi demand is expected to keep Saudi capacity busy first; North America supply from Saudi is not ruled out. Jordan was a strategic decision based on reconstruction in Syria, Iraq and Lebanon.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi utilisation ramp in FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aiming for at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year of operations, with a fast ramp if the supply chain stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US order margin locked in through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed yes, the margins on the existing US orders are locked in.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 outperform the INR2,850 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would love to but is cautious given uncontrollable variables; it expects to meet or exceed guidance based on past delivery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the India domestic outlook and the net debt position after capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic demand may stay sluggish for several quarters, especially in water; the company remains in net cash of about INR3,800 crore even after all announced capex.

risks_watch: Middle East supply chain and freight disruption delaying Saudi order materialisation and export shipments.
Slower US ordering as customers calibrate timing; data-centre pipeline moderated in the last month per management.
Weak India domestic water and DI demand (Jal Jeevan Mission budget slowdown); domestic bid pipeline described as a concern.
Rising competition in Saudi Arabia from peers with new capacity, and possible delays in capacity ramp.
Deployment of a growing cash pile (net cash INR3,887 crore) under the Board-approved capital allocation policy, with no specific plan announced.
Sintex losses increased and Welspun Specialty export weakness to Europe.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the US and Saudi medium-term demand and on the record financials, but cautious on near-term India domestic demand and Middle East logistics. Management was reluctant to commit beyond the FY27 guidance and to quantify the bid pipeline, and deferred the capital allocation split to later.
key_quotes: Our Q2 FY27 EBITDA stood at a record all-time high of INR782 crores, registering 25% year-on-year growth.
We are currently booked through F Y29 in the U.S.
Now the order materialization, the business materialization may take some time because of the conditions.
So we are very, very clear about it. And if you see in the H1, we have been able to deliver what we have committed.

adds.what: US spiral pipe debottlenecking, +225,000 MTPA at Little Rock
Saudi LSAW and DI pipe plants (final commissioning)
Jordan spiral pipe and coating JV with Perma-Pipe, 350,000-500,000 t/yr (up to USD 125 million)
India FBE coating JV with Perma-Pipe at Anjar (about INR110 crore)

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR2,850 crore was held (not raised) and H1 EBITDA is up 30%, with a ~INR50,000 crore order book and US booked through FY29 backing near-term growth; domestic India demand is weak, and new US/Saudi/Jordan capacity only contributes from FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA up 30% YoY to INR1,538 crore with US order margins locked in through FY29, but FY27 guidance of INR2,850 crore was only held and domestic DI volumes are set to fall substantially.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Saudi LSAW and DIP plants are in final commissioning for Q3 FY27 with ramp by year-end, and the India FBE JV is due operational in the next financial year (about INR110 crore); US debottlenecking (+225,000 MTPA) is ready by March 2028 and Jordan (350,000-500,000 t) is later.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book near INR50,000 crore (USD 5.2 billion) with US booked through FY29 and exports robust, but Saudi order materialisation is delayed and India domestic volumes will be substantially lower, and incremental earnings from new capacity only start in FY28.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board has approved three new investments (US debottlenecking up to USD 115 million, Jordan JV up to USD 125 million, India FBE JV about INR110 crore) while H1 FY27 capex was about INR1,500 crore; further allocation of the INR3,887 crore net cash is deferred with no specific plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said H2 is tracking well and it would be pleasantly surprised to exceed INR2,850 crore EBITDA guidance, but stayed cautious on uncontrollable variables after H1 EBITDA of INR1,538 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Middle East supply chain and freight disruption could delay Saudi order materialisation and exports, and US ordering is being calibrated with the data-centre pipeline moderating in the last month.

rows.label: US demand visibility through FY29 and beyond
rows.why: US booked through FY29 with a INR5,500 crore data-centre pipeline order won recently, and management expects demand to last 3 to 5 years beyond FY29, though ordering intensity will slow.

rows.label: Saudi utilisation ramp to 50-60% in year one
rows.why: Management targets at least 50-60% utilisation in the first year, with a fast ramp if the supply chain stabilises, but order materialisation has been delayed by Middle East disruption.

rows.label: Saudi anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports
rows.why: Management noted anti-dumping duty on DI pipe imports in Saudi Arabia, with about two-thirds of captive DI requirement served by imports, supporting Welspun's first right of refusal on local demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on US and Saudi medium-term demand, record financials and 22.7% ROCE, but cautious on near-term India domestic water demand, Middle East logistics and FY27 guidance; analysts pressed on US order intensity beyond FY29, Saudi utilisation and the use of the net cash pile.
